description: R05 TerminalCore reconciliation overlay. Exact is reserved for source methods reproduced materially in safe Rust; Partial records real migrated subsets; retained WinRT helper mechanics remain platform/UI boundaries rather than fabricated Rust product types.

entries.notes: Single-cell anchor and rendered span are reproduced directly.
Linear start/end geometry and one-span representation are reproduced directly.
Block selection produces one horizontal span for every selected row with the same bounds.
Anchoring on a wide glyph's leading cell remains degenerate at the leading cell.
Word expansion selects the complete populated word and keeps a right-exclusive end.
Double-clicking the empty/control class expands across the entire row from zero to RightExclusive.
Regular, delimiter and control classes remain distinct; clicking the isolated > delimiter selects only that cell.
Line expansion follows forced-wrap rows and ends at the right-exclusive boundary of the final logical row.
Forward/backward dragging and Shift+Click preserve the immutable pivot and right-exclusive forward Char endpoint.
Microsoft itself documents this as a XAML UI-thread event that cannot run in the ordinary unit-test host; managed/UI ownership is intentionally retained.

sourceRules.notes: Rust TerminalInput owns portable modifier/key translation, but Terminal::SendCharEvent Alt+Shift casing and the exact invalid-VK SendKeyEvent guard are not both reproduced through the TerminalCore aggregate.
No safe Rust Terminal aggregate currently owns CreateFromSettings/UserResize history+viewport clamping to SHRT_MAX. TextBuffer dimensions alone are not an honest replacement for this terminal policy.
Scroll-position callbacks, buffer-circling notification policy and renderer TriggerScroll invalidation still belong to the native Terminal/renderer integration surface.

Selection geometry is materially migrated, but viewport-relative input clamping, trailing-wide-glyph anchor expansion, wide-glyph block-span repair and scrolled viewport translation are not yet equivalent for every Microsoft source method.

Parser/adapter boundaries for color, cursor and OSC actions are represented in Rust. Terminal-owned hyperlink tables, taskbar state, working-directory state and the complete aggregate write path remain outside terminal-core ownership.
Rust owns buffer rows/reflow and several parser/adapter boundaries, but the complete Terminal write/snap-to-output/tab-stop/URL-pattern aggregate is not yet represented by one Rust owner.

til::property/event/typed_event are C++/WinRT compatibility helpers at the retained native boundary. Recreating those helper types in Rust solely for test count parity would violate the migration ownership policy.
